subject: Startups
title: Burn Rate and Runway
description: A fast breakdown of Burn Rate and Runway for builders.

hook.text: Burn rate is how fast your startup spends money each month. Runway is how many months until the money runs out.

buildup.text: If you have $3M in the bank and burn $200K per month, your runway is 15 months. Simple but existential.

discovery.text: Investors want at least 18–24 months of runway after a raise. Less than 6 months triggers panic fundraising.

twist.text: Net burn (spending minus revenue) is more useful than gross burn. Growing revenue extends runway automatically.

climax.text: Runway isn't just math—it's options. More months mean more time to find product-market fit or raise the next round.

punchline.text: Runway is time. Time is the startup's most precious resource.

quiz.question: How is runway calculated?
options: Cash in bank divided by monthly burn rate
